# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b16 - General sources, Home hub and smarter delivery

This opt-in beta completes the General settings and Home-level behavior requested after the rooms-first setup changes. Stable **v0.5.1** remains unchanged and this prerelease is never marked Latest. Existing config-entry, entity, room and managed-controller identities are preserved; do not delete and recreate the integration.

## First-run General source defaults

On the first General settings pass, every discovered **weather** entity and eligible **outdoor air-quality** entity is preselected. All discovered pollen provider sensors are also selected, allowing multiple providers rather than silently retaining only one. These are first-run conveniences only: once the user explicitly saves an empty or narrower selection, that choice remains authoritative on later edits.

Pollen evaluation remains provider-specific and conservative. The integration does not compare unlike provider scales as if they were interchangeable; it records each selected provider and uses the worst normalized valid selected reading for the aggregate recommendation. Missing or stale selected providers remain visible as unavailable evidence.

## Announcement Hub and Task AI

The **Enable Announcement Hub** field is shown only when Announcement Hub has a configured Home Assistant entry. Enabling the option does not make Home Environment Manager pick physical speakers or notification devices; Hub remains the routing, occupancy, queue and recovery authority when it is available.

The AI provider selector now includes both Home Assistant conversation agents and data-capable **AI Task** entities. Selecting an `ai_task.*` entity sends direct rewrite requests through Home Assistant's `ai_task.generate_data` action with the selected entity, a named task and the same bounded rewrite instructions used for conversation agents. Returned Task AI text passes the existing action/room/window/reason/numeric grounding validation. Provider errors, invalid output or timeout return the original deterministic announcement instead of suppressing it. When an announcement is handed to Announcement Hub, the selected AI entity is passed to Hub so Hub can apply its own Task-AI semantics.

## Provider-aware TTS languages

The TTS language field no longer exposes internal source-style labels. It reads the selected TTS entity's real supported-language capability and displays human language names. If a provider exposes only one variant, the label stays simple, for example **Deutsch**. A region is shown only when that provider exposes multiple variants of the same language, for example **English (US)** and **English (UK)**. Unsupported integration languages are not fabricated, and changing the selected TTS engine revalidates the saved language against that provider.

## Native Home group and global entities

Home-wide settings and outputs are now assigned to a native **Home** configuration group and the existing Home Environment Manager Home device. The recommendation/dashboard sensor, global thresholds, announcement controls, language, occupancy policy, AQI/pollen settings and other home-level entities therefore no longer appear unassigned. Room groups still contain their room-wide settings plus one managed controller per selected physical product. Existing registry IDs and user customizations are migrated in place.

## Nobody-home cooldown

A fresh explicitly empty occupied-room list is now treated as positive evidence that nobody is home. A fresh set of room-presence sensors where all selected sensors are OFF is handled the same way. **Away is not applied immediately**: the Home device exposes a configurable away cooldown in minutes. Until the cooldown expires, the home remains in the home profile. Unknown, unavailable, stale, malformed or unrecognized room evidence stays unknown and never starts Away.

This global cooldown complements each room's existing unoccupied delay. It does not bypass device ownership, manual/restart pauses, minimum ON/OFF dwell, open-window interlocks, feedback freshness or independent physical protection. Physical HVAC/compressor/fan safety requirements remain the user's responsibility and are not certified by software tests.

## Validation and installation

Publication is gated by the full Python 3.13 and 3.14 regression suite, deterministic regeneration of all 38 language catalogs, frontend tests, Hassfest and HACS. Additional isolated checks run against installed **Home Assistant 2026.10.0** and verify real config subentries/device registries, the Home + room hierarchy, rooms-first selectors, read-only config-entry settings and controller behavior. These tests do not operate the user's live installation or physical equipment.

Install via HACS with beta versions enabled, choose **v0.6.0b16**, restart Home Assistant and keep the existing integration entry. Review General settings once to confirm the automatically selected weather/outdoor/pollen sources, then adjust the Home away cooldown and delivery/AI/TTS choices as desired.
